label: third original token (t=2), esp. e, with a favorable first token
explanation: Position-locked unit: about 80% of activation mass is at step t=2 (the third original token). It never fires at t=0,1,4 or at t=6-10. Smaller pockets: t=3 (original token 3, or <DEL> when L=3), t=5, and late copy steps (t=11-17), which together hold about 20% of mass. At t=2, whether it fires depends additively on token identities. Input e is the strongest (rate about 0.9 at t=2, about half of all mass, and most of the top activations), then v, m, t, u, q, k, 1, b. It fires more when the first token is z/o/r/i/s/l/k/m and the previous token is w/c/d/a. A binary predicate cannot capture this graded additive token code, so precision and recall stay moderate (dev F1 0.62, mass recall 0.69). Top activations are t=2 inputs of e (or t/m) in short sequences. It is weak or absent on digits 0/2/3 and w at t=2.
